title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). A is a commutative ring and C is an A-linear category. A functor F: C → C' is 'admissible' if it commutes with external tensor products P⊗_o X, where o is an A-algebra acting on X. The 'Deuring' case is the one where C has a 'strict generator' X: every object is P⊗_o X with P a finitely generated projective right o-module and o = End_C(X). Grothendieck defines C(1) = Hom_{A-adm}(C^o, Mod(A)) and the fully faithful Yoneda functor i: C → C(1), X ↦ Hom_C(−, X).

This page. Put F = i(X), so F(Y) = Hom(Y, X). Grothendieck asserts that for every object Y, F(Y) is a finitely generated projective module over (End Y)^o, the endomorphism algebra of Y in C^o. He then defines C_sp(1) as the full subcategory of admissible presheaves F such that every value F(Y) is finitely generated projective over (End Y)^o. A later insertion names the general case 'primaires'. Yoneda gives an inclusion C ⊂ C_sp(1), with the caveat 'subject to the existence of generators'.

Choosing a strict generator X identifies C_sp(1) with proj(o), the category of finitely generated projective right o-modules. The identification is evaluation at X, inverse to P ↦ P⊗_o X. In modern terms C_sp(1) is the idempotent (Karoubi) / additive completion of C, equivalently its Cauchy completion: the absolute or 'small-projective' presheaves. C itself embeds in proj(End X) as the full subcategory of those P for which P⊗_o X exists.

The name he finally adopts is uncertain. A struck-out phrase reads 'saturé projectif', which is plausibly what the subscript 'sp' abbreviates. It is replaced by something like 'simplifié (ou pseudo-saturé)', i.e. a pseudo-abelian / Karoubian envelope. The bottom-left margin is a programmatic note: avoid finiteness hypotheses and say everywhere 'locally free of finite rank over S = Spec A' instead of 'projective of finite type'.

Purpose. This is preparation for a Galois / Tannakian-type theory of motives over a base ring A. It sets up the formal completion of an A-linear category of motives, linearised by its endomorphism algebras, which is what Deuring-style isogeny categories need.
errors: The claim that Hom(Y,X) is finitely generated projective over End(Y) for every Y does not follow just from Y = P⊗_o X with P finitely generated projective. Then Hom(Y,X) ≅ Hom_o(P,o), and as an End_o(P)-module this need not be projective. Counterexample: a finite-dimensional algebra with indecomposable projectives P1, P2 such that End(P1) = k[x]/x^2 and Hom(P1,P2) = k. Grothendieck evidently notices this: the next page adds the 'jolie' axiom that Hom(X,X') be finitely generated projective over O' with O' as commutant. On this page the statement needs the Deuring / 'primaire' hypothesis (e.g. semisimple endomorphism algebras).
'pour tout objet Y de X' is a slip for 'de C'.
Left/right and opposite-ring conventions are loose: Hom(Y,X) is naturally a right End(Y)-module, i.e. a left module over End(Y)^o. It is called 'à droite ... sous o'^o' here.

ideas.what: Category of admissible A-linear presheaves whose values are finitely generated projective over the endomorphism algebras; the Yoneda embedding of C into it.
ideas.modern_name: Cauchy completion / idempotent (Karoubi) completion of an A-linear category; absolute or small-projective presheaves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Karoubi (1960s), Lawvere (Cauchy completion, 1973); pseudo-abelian envelope in motives via Grothendieck's school (Manin 1968, Demazure 1969)
ideas.where_published: Pseudo-abelian envelope of correspondences appears in expositions of Grothendieck's motives (Manin, Demazure, Kleiman), not in a Grothendieck-authored text that I can name

ideas.what: A strict generator X identifies the completion with finitely generated projective right End(X)-modules via P ↦ P⊗_o X.
ideas.modern_name: Morita theory / Morita equivalence for additive categories with a generator

ideas.what: Working relative to S = Spec A with 'locally free of finite rank' replacing 'projective of finite type'.
ideas.modern_name: Linear categories over a base scheme / A-linear Tannakian framework

missed.claim: Grothendieck's own term 'Catégories de Deuring' (with variants 'primaire', 'saturé projectif'/'pseudo-saturé', and 'jolie' on the next page) for A-linear categories Morita-equivalent to proj(End X). This is a 1965 axiomatic precursor of the linear-category framework in the theory of motives. The mathematics is standard Morita / Karoubi completion, but the terminology and its motivic purpose are not in the record.
missed.quote: le choix d'un strict X de C permet d'identifier C_sp(1) à la catégorie des O-modules à droite projectifs de type fini
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical only: it documents an early, base-ring-relative formulation of the Karoubian / Cauchy completion of motive categories within the 'Galois theory of motives' notes.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the Morita / Karoubi (Cauchy) completion of an A-linear category with a generator. It is standard, and the projectivity claim needs the extra 'jolie' axiom that Grothendieck adds on the next page. The only point of interest is historical terminology and context.
transcription_corrections: 'pour tout objet Y de X' — the manuscript has X, but the sense requires 'de C'.
'O° où O = End(Y)' is better read as o'^o, o' = End(Y), a primed algebra distinct from o = End(X).
The struck-out word read as 'Cfd' is uncertain.
The struck phrase before '(ou pseudo-saturé)' appears to be 'saturé projectif'. This suggests the subscript 'sp' = 'saturé projectif'. The superscript replacement read as 'simplifié' is doubtful.
The bottom-left margin is likely: 'il faut éviter l'hypothèse de finitude : on dira partout loc. libre de rang fini sur Spec A = S'.
